deliverables: Upgrade Cardano mainnet protocol to major version 11 and minor version 0 while remaining in the Conway era.
Make new Plutus primitives from CIP-0109, CIP-0132, CIP-0133, CIP-0138, and CIP-0153 available.
Make all Plutus built-in functions available consistently across Plutus V1, V2, and V3.
Add UPLC case expressions for Bool, Integer, and Data.
Promote or tighten ledger validation rules including VRF key hash uniqueness, reference input rules, Constitutional Committee voting restrictions, and withdrawal validation.
Improve Cardano node PPView mismatch diagnostics.
request.what: Initiate an intra-era Cardano mainnet hard fork to Protocol Version 11 minor version 0, called the van Rossem hard fork.

claims.claim: The proposal would upgrade Cardano mainnet from protocol version 10.0 to protocol version 11.0 without an era transition.

The upgrade introduces new Plutus functionality defined in CIP-0109, CIP-0132, CIP-0133, CIP-0138, and CIP-0153, including modular exponentiation, dropList, BLS12-381 multi-scalar multiplication, Array, and Value built-ins.
All Plutus built-in functions, including newly introduced ones, will become available across Plutus V1, V2, and V3 after the hard fork.

The proposal states that testing reports demonstrate no behavioral regressions, complete conformance between specification and implementation for new ledger rules, and correct operation of new Plutus primitives and case expressions across Plutus V1, V2, and V3.

The linked Cardano Node 11.0.1 performance report is cited as showing no regressions for standard value, Plutus, and voting benchmarks and acceptable baseline performance for the new primitives and case expressions.
The proposal states that security audits have been undertaken for Plutus BLS primitives and execution costs for all Plutus primitives.

At least 85% of stake pools by active stake should have upgraded to a node version capable of supporting protocol version 11 before ratification, and this readiness must be verified by the Constitutional Committee and SPOs with support from Intersect's Hard Fork Working Group reports.

The proposal states the hard fork is consistent with all eight relevant constitutional hard-fork guardrails, while noting HARDFORK-04 depends on stake pool upgrade status before ratification and none of the guardrails can be checked by the automated guardrails script.

The hard fork is described as a permanent change to on-chain ledger rules whose reversion is only possible in extreme circumstances through the CIP-0135 disaster recovery process, with Plutus primitive use potentially disabled through companion cost model settings if issues are found.
The proposal states that Intersect's Hard Fork Working Group recommended submitting the governance action on 2026-06-15 and Intersect's Technical Steering Committee endorsed it on 2026-06-16.

summary: The document proposes a non-treasury hard fork to Cardano protocol version 11.0, focused on Plutus capability and performance, ledger-rule consistency, and node diagnostics, with cited CIPs and one performance report but limited risk-detail evidence in the text.
